title: What If You Ate Nothing but Sugar for a Month?

scenes.text: What if you ate nothing but sugar? You'd have plenty of energy. And you'd still be starving.
Sugar is pure calories: no protein, fat or vitamins. The WHO says under 10 percent of your energy. This is 100.
Within a few weeks your thiamine is gone; the body barely stores it, and carbs burn it faster. Tingling hands, wasting muscle: beriberi.
Within a month, scurvy. With almost no vitamin C, the signs appear in about four weeks. Untreated, scurvy is fatal.
A can of soda holds up to 40 grams of sugar. Your whole day would be about twelve cans' worth.
Calories can't fix a body that's missing everything else. Full, and starving at the same time.

description:
What if you ate nothing but sugar? Sugar supplies calories but no protein, fat, vitamins or minerals. The World Health Organization recommends keeping free sugars below 10 percent of daily energy, ideally 5 percent, about 25 grams, while a single can of soda can hold 40 grams. The body stores little thiamine, and a high-carbohydrate diet raises the need for it, so reserves can run out within a few weeks, bringing the tingling, numbness and muscle loss of beriberi. With vitamin C intake below about 10 milligrams a day, signs of scurvy can appear within a month, and untreated scurvy is fatal.

first_comment: Sailors on old voyages got scurvy from biscuit and salt meat, and limes fixed it. Which single food would you pick if you had to eat only one?
